definition: A regulated market is one where a government-appointed commission oversees a state-sanctioned monopoly over part of the energy market; a deregulated market removes that legislative monopoly to allow competing participants, though substantial government oversight typically remains.
core_idea: Deregulation is about permitting competition, not eliminating regulation — most deregulated power markets remain heavily regulated in practice.
key_points: Regulated market: public utility/public service commission oversees a state monopoly
Deregulated market: legislative barriers to competition are removed
Deregulated markets still carry substantial government oversight
relationships: Underlies why RTO/ISO markets allow free electricity trading but remain rule-heavy
trading_implications: Market rules and participant eligibility vary by jurisdiction even within deregulated markets, so local rules must be checked per grid
caveats: Deregulated does not mean unregulated — significant oversight persists
